newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to sell off state water utilities in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to sell off state water utilities in 1997.

text.p: Brazil will privatise regional water utilities next year and is prepared to finance foreign firms in exchange for investing in local infrastructure, said an official at the National Development Bank (BNDES).

"Our objective is to finance private concessionaries," BNDES vice-president and privatisation director Jose Pio Borges told reporters. "We will give concessions to private firms in order to obtain an investment commitment."
Thirteen states have been given the green light to proceed with a variety of privatisations next year and water sanitation would be a key sector in the drive, Borges said.
Two states already launched their privatisations this year. Rio Grande do Sul sold a 35 percent stake in state telecommunications firm CRT while Rio de Janeiro auctioned off its power utility Cerj.

"(Sanitation) is very different from the electricity sector, which has an intrinsic value," he said. "Here, the interest is not in raising revenue but in increasing private investment and improving standards."
Borges said French water utility Compagnie Generale des Eaux and Britain's Anglian Water had expressed an interest in investing in Brazilian state water sanitation companies.
Both companies were already involved in joint projects with Brazilian firms, he added.
Brazil will follow the model of Argentina and Mexico to develop a case-by-case approach to privatising its own water utilities, Borges said.
